title: compact-instrumentation-playbook-sessionization-dashboard-prioritization
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact working playbook for instrumenting sessionization, selecting a minimal but effective signal set, and prioritizing dashboard surfaces for rapid operator investigations during model rollouts and runtime fallback events. The goal is to produce a small, high-signal telemetry footprint that keeps query cost bounded while enabling fast root-cause.

Context / motivation:
- We observed long investigation times for multi-hop requests where token-level fanout interacts with KV-cache misses.
- Current dashboards are rich but noisy; operators waste time chasing false-positive spikes.
- Need a template that teams can copy for new models or rollout gates (hosted, dedicated, private) and that ties directly to oncall playbooks.

Non-goals:
- This doc does not attempt to enumerate every metric for every model. It prescribes a compact, prioritized surface and sampling strategy.
- Not a replacement for full audit logs or slow-path traces for compliance-only requests.

Core principles (short):
- Signal-first: pick metrics that reduce investigation branches (latency, cold-cache, fallback-rate, token-efficiency).
- Cost-aware sampling: aggressive low-cost aggregates with targeted high-fidelity traces only on guardrail triggers.
- Sessionization as primary key: reconstruct operator view from session id -> request id -> span chain.
- Dashboard triage lanes: one-line cause inference (cache / model / infra / client) within 5 clicks.

Minimal metric set (definitions + rationale):
- user_session_duration_ms (p90/p99): elapsed time between session.start and session.end events. Rationale: surface UX impact and multi-call latencies.
- request_ttf_token_ms (p50/p95/p99): time to first token emitted per request. Flags slow model cold-starts.
- overall_token_latency_ms (p50/p90/p99): per-token generation latency measured in the runtime (includes kernel scheduling). Shows token cost/latency.
- kv_cache_hit_rate (percent, weighted by token count): measured on model container. Primary signal to detect cold-cache storms.
- fallback_invocations_per_min (count, by route/model-variant): includes automatic fallback to cheaper/robust variant. Key SLA/quality guard.
- model_response_quality_score (sampled, 1-5): periodic sampled human or regression op measure, ties to eval sets. Use sparingly.
- route_concurrency (gauge): concurrent outstanding requests per route to monitor queuing/backpressure.
- error_class_summary (count by class): aggregate by high-level classes (validation, infra, model-runtime, downstream). Helps triage.

Tracing design (span taxonomy and sampling):
- Primary span roots: session.span -> request.span -> model.call.span -> runtime-kernel.span -> kv-access.span -> external-io.span
- Span fields to standardize: session_id, request_id, route, model_variant, tenant_id, kv_key_hint (hashed), token_offset_on_request, cpu_gpu_affinity (for dedicated). Keep PII off.
- Sampling rules:
  - Default: 0.2% global trace sampling to keep costs low.
  - Increase to 100% for requests that: trigger fallback; exceed ttf threshold (configurable per model); produce 5xx error_class_summary; or explicitly flagged by client.
  - Adaptive burst sampling: when kv_cache_hit_rate drops >10% relative to baseline AND overall_token_latency_ms p95 rises, ramp traces to 10% for 15 minutes.
- Trace size limits: cap per-request spans to 50 spans and 200KB of annotations to prevent storage blowup. Drop low-value annotations (raw prompt texts) from sampled traces; store prompt fingerprints only.

Dashboard prioritization (layout prescriptions):
- Top row (ops guardrails): request rate, route_concurrency, overall_token_latency_ms p95, fallback_invocations_per_min. Aim: answer "is system overloaded or falling back?"
- Second row (cache and model health): kv_cache_hit_rate, model_response_quality_score (sample), model_variant_error_rate. Aim: separate cache vs model issues.
- Third row (investigation starters): session_slices (search by session_id), top request_ttf_token_ms contributors, error_class_summary by route. Aim: 1-click to session traces and recent requests.
- Drilldowns: each panel must link directly to (1) trace view filtered by request_id, (2) recent raw operator logs for the session_id, (3) underlying infra metrics for the host pool.
- Alerting: alerts SHOULD target narrow conditions and include runbook link and sample request_id. Examples: 
  - Fallback spike alert: fallback_invocations_per_min > baseline*3 for 5m -> severity P1.
  - Cold-cache storm alert: kv_cache_hit_rate drop > 15% and request_ttf_token_ms p95 increase > 200ms -> severity P2.
  - Token-latency runup: overall_token_latency_ms p99 rise > 2x baseline for 3m excluding canary models -> P2.

Operator playbook (triage flow):
1) Check Top row: rate/concurrency/latency/fallback. If rate is stable but latency/breakdown changes, suspect cache/model.
2) Check kv_cache_hit_rate and kv-access spans. If hit_rate low -> inspect recent model updates and cache eviction logs.
3) If fallback rate high, inspect model_variant_error_rate and trace samples for error_class_summary.
4) If none of above, escalate to infra: check node-level CPU/GPU saturation and network errors.

Implementation checklist (MVP):
- [ ] Define standardized session_id header in API gateway (ticket: OBS-1793).
- [ ] Implement session start/end events in SDK and runtime.
- [ ] Add kv_cache_hit_rate instrumentation in model-side metrics (PR: #402).
- [ ] Add lightweight trace annotations: request_id, session_id, route, model_variant.
- [ ] Dashboard: build top-row panels, add drill-to-trace links.
- [ ] Alerts + runbooks: configure three initial alerts and attach runbooks.

Cost-control notes:
- Prefer aggregate counters and percentiles over full-text logs.
- Use hashed prompt fingerprints for indexing rather than storing prompt text in telemetry.
- Keep trace retention short (30 days default for sampled traces) and archive longer-term only for releases.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How granular should kv cache keys be in traces? (privacy vs debug value). Proposed: store hashed key plus categorical key hint only.
- Do we want tenant-weighted SLOs surfaced on the main dashboards or as a separate tenant-ops view?
- Rolling canary telemetry: should canary runs have separate sampling/stretch for higher fidelity? (suggestion: yes, 100% sampling for canary cohort).

Next steps & owners:
- Evelyn: finalize session_id header spec and post to Confluence (due 2025-02-20).
- Marco: instrument kv_cache_hit_rate + normalize metric name and units (due 2025-02-28).
- Aisha: dashboard skeleton + drill links (due 2025-03-05).

Notes-to-self / rough ideas:
- Consider quick synthetic probe that warms KV caches for largest tenants ahead of traffic surges.
- Add a microdash that only SREs see with a compact 6-panel triage view.

References / links:
- Confluence: Sessionization Primer (linked above).
- GitHub: PR #402 (kv instrumentation).
- Jira: OBS-1789 (dashboard refactor).

Comments welcome — this is intentionally compact. We should pair with oncall for a 30-minute walkthrough once the dashboard skeleton exists.
